read: full: abstract, sections 1-5 (pp. 1-10), Appendix A.1-A.6 and B (pp. 16-24); skimmed Table 1 (p17), the o1 examples (pp. 19-21) and the references
venue_now: ICLR 2025 ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', p1 header); the file is arXiv:2410.05229v2 of 27 Aug 2025 (p1). The May entry cites the arXiv preprint.
what_it_is: GSM-Symbolic turns 100 questions from the GSM8K test set into symbolic templates: the authors mark the names and numbers as variables with value domains and conditions (e.g. divisibility) that keep question and answer valid, and the template also instantiates the worked solution (Fig. 1 p2; p4). Each template yields 50 instances, giving 50 sets of 100 questions (5,000 per benchmark), and accuracy is reported as a distribution over the sets (p5). Variants change difficulty by removing or adding clauses (GSM-M1, GSM-P1, GSM-P2) and add a seemingly relevant but inconsequential clause (GSM-NoOp) (pp. 7-9). Across 25 open and closed models, final-answer accuracy varies across instantiations of the same questions, falls more when numbers change than when only names change, falls and spreads as clauses are added, and drops by 17.5 to 65.7 points on GSM-NoOp (pp. 5-10).
domain: grade-school arithmetic word problems (the four basic operations; p4)
size: 100 templates from GSM8K test items; 50 instances each, i.e. 50 sets of 100 and 5,000 questions per variant; five variants (M1, Symbolic, P1, P2, NoOp) (pp. 5, 7-9); 25 models, more than 20 open models of 2B to 27B plus GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini and o1-preview (pp. 2, 5); nearly 500 evaluations (p5)
source_of_items: generated from templates, which were hand-annotated from existing GSM8K test questions (pp. 4-5); the harder and NoOp variants are further templates edited from these (pp. 7, 9)
instances: generated (50 instantiations per template with new names and numbers; the number of samples can be raised by widening variable domains, p5)
has_gold_traces: yes: each template carries the GSM8K-style worked solution, with calculator annotations, instantiated with the sampled values (Fig. 1, p2); the generated solutions serve as few-shot examples in the NoOp-Symb experiment (p9) but are not used for scoring.
evaluation: final answer: accuracy under 8-shot chain-of-thought prompting with greedy decoding (pp. 5, 16), reported as a distribution over the 50 generated sets (p5). One ablation extracts the equations a model writes and checks that both sides agree, to measure arithmetic accuracy (Table 2, p23); this is an analysis, not part of the benchmark's scoring, and no step is otherwise judged.
human_validation: Template construction: annotation of variables, domains and conditions (who annotated is not stated), then automatic checks that no original value remains in the template, that the original values satisfy the conditions and that the final answer matches the original (pp. 4-5). Generated data: 10 random samples per template reviewed manually; any question that fewer than two models answer correctly is reviewed manually again (p5). No agreement statistics and no human evaluation of model outputs.
contamination_measures: generated instances with new names and numbers (pp. 4-5). The paper reads GSM8K scores that sit above the GSM-Symbolic distribution (21 of 25 models) as a sign of possible contamination (p6). Templates and generated data are public (p1).

engtrace_use.sentence: S-M1: 'In mathematics, benchmarks ranging from GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) and Math (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) to HardMath (Fan et al., 2024), Putnam-Axiom (Gulati et al., 2024), and GSM-Symbolic (Mirzadeh et al., 2024) rigorously test abstract logical deduction and reasoning stability.' S-I2 (Introduction): 'Symbolic templates (Mirzadeh et al., 2024; Xie et al., 2025) serve as the generative mechanism, producing unique, contamination-resistant instances'
engtrace_use.explanation: S-M1: 'reasoning stability' is exactly what GSM-Symbolic measures: the spread of accuracy across instantiations of the same questions (pp. 5-6), sensitivity to changed numbers against changed names (p7), the effect of added clauses (p8) and of irrelevant ones (pp. 9-10). The paper frames its subject as 'genuine logical reasoning' against pattern matching (pp. 1, 3), so 'logical deduction' follows its own framing, though 'abstract' fits grade-school arithmetic word problems loosely (p4). S-I2: GSM-Symbolic is the right precedent for symbolic templates as the generative mechanism (Fig. 1, p2; p4), and it motivates them by the contamination risk of a single static test set (pp. 2, 4). Two caveats for the rewrite. First, GSM-Symbolic does not claim its own instances are contamination-resistant; it releases templates and generated data publicly (p1) and uses generation to measure variance and fragility. Second, its templates already instantiate a worked solution with every instance (Fig. 1, p2), so pairing instances with gold solutions is not what EngTrace adds over it; what EngTrace adds is using the gold trace to evaluate steps, since GSM-Symbolic scores final answers only (pp. 5, 16).

suggested_wording: GSM-Symbolic (Mirzadeh et al., 2025) turns 100 GSM8K test questions into symbolic templates that instantiate both question and worked solution, and shows that final-answer accuracy varies across instantiations of the same question, falls when the numbers change or clauses are added, and drops sharply when an irrelevant clause is inserted.
facts_to_cite: GSM-Symbolic templates are built from 100 GSM8K test questions by marking names and numbers as variables with value domains and validity conditions; the template also instantiates the worked solution (Fig. 1, p2; p4).
Each template generates 50 instances, giving 50 sets of 100 questions, and accuracy is reported as a distribution over the sets (p5).
Templates were checked automatically, 10 random generated samples per template were reviewed manually, and any question fewer than two models answered correctly was reviewed again (pp. 4-5).
25 open and closed models were evaluated with 8-shot chain-of-thought and greedy decoding (pp. 2, 5, 16).
Accuracy varies across instantiations of the same questions, e.g. a worst-to-best gap of more than 12 points for Gemma2-9B and about 15 for Phi-3.5-mini (pp. 5-6).
Changing numbers lowers accuracy more than changing only names (Fig. 4, p7); adding clauses lowers accuracy and widens its spread (GSM-M1 to GSM-P2, Fig. 6, p8).
Inserting a seemingly relevant but inconsequential clause (GSM-NoOp) lowers accuracy by 17.5 (o1-preview) to 65.7 (Phi-3-mini) points (Fig. 8a, p10).
The authors concede that under the statistical assumptions of Ivanova et al. (2025) the drop from GSM8K to GSM-Symbolic is not significant (pp. 18, 23-24).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: symbolic templates with typed variables, value ranges and validity conditions that generate many instances per item (Fig. 1, p4), the mechanism EngTrace uses; a worked solution instantiated with each instance (Fig. 1); reporting a distribution over instances rather than one score (p5), as EngTrace reports within- and between-template spread; difficulty varied by adding clauses (pp. 7-8); and a test of superficial changes with the numbers fixed (names only, p7), close in purpose to EngTrace's paraphrase arm. Lacks: an engineering or physical domain (grade-school arithmetic, p4); step-level evaluation (final-answer accuracy only, pp. 5, 16; the instantiated solutions are never used to score steps); templates written from scratch (they derive from 100 public GSM8K test items, pp. 4-5); validation of the evaluator against experts; and a private pool (templates and generated data are public, p1).
notes: Reference: the May entry (L1096-1100) prints 'Kiarash Alizadeh' and 'Hidetoshi Shahrokhi'; the authors are Keivan Alizadeh and Hooman Shahrokhi (p1). The paper is now ICLR 2025 (p1 header), so the entry and in-text year should change. Statistical caveat: the significance test behind the GSM8K-to-GSM-Symbolic drop is a one-sample t-test, and Appendix A.3 and B concede that under Ivanova et al. (2025) the results are not significant (pp. 18, 23-24); the revised text should rest on the variance, the clause-count trend and GSM-NoOp rather than on the drop. Minor inconsistency: the text says the performance of all models drops on GSM-Symbolic (p2), but Figure 2 shows Llama3-8b-instruct at 74.6 on GSM-Symbolic against 74.0 on the 100 originals (p6). Bearing on the May section 3.2 ('templates go beyond variable substitution'): within a GSM-Symbolic template only names and numbers vary under arithmetic conditions (p4); the harder and NoOp variants are separate, edited templates (pp. 7, 9). The revised text should say concretely what EngTrace's templates add rather than imply that GSM-Symbolic varies only numbers. The verdict is the same for both sentences.
